result.title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
result.summary: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization (BO) evaluates candidates in resumable increments but usually stops at a budget or convergence test. We maximize a budget-free utility, the best observed score minus a cost per increment, with a one-step lookahead: advance the candidate with the largest expected improvement (EI) under a fixed surrogate, and stop once no EI exceeds the cost. This rule, EI stopping, never falls below stopping immediately in expected utility, yet it can stop too early. We construct a certificate, a lower bound on the value of two-step lookahead, that proves such a stop premature, and repeating this correction never lowers expected utility under the surrogate. Under the surrogate, EI stops are premature on average at low costs and lose little at high costs. On three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, a pre-registered test finds EI stopping noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction gains at low costs on two of the three; more information sharing in the surrogate raises EI stopping's utility. On the surrogates of two published methods, EI stopping trades lower scores for fewer training increments. EI stopping is a simple cost-aware reference whose utility depends on the surrogate.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 freeze-thaw 贝叶斯优化中的成本感知停止：以「最佳观测分数减去每次增量成本」为无预算效用，提出仅在期望改进（EI）超过成本时继续的 EI 停止规则，并构造一个两步前瞻价值下界的证明书来判定该停止是否过早，在三个超参数优化基准上做了预注册比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「单步前瞻何时足够」、效用中显式减去增量成本、以及判定停止过早的下界证明，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的停止决策与动态计算收益核算提供形式化参照，但需核查代理模型假设能否对应推理状态与证据获取。
